ticket.description:
# KS-1229 X-ISSUE-LOOSE - Wednesday's task for Ornith, JEST (ts-jest), **TEST-ONLY MODE, MODIFY THE EXISTING TEST IN PLACE** (one hunk) (written 04:09 AEST on 2026-09-18)

Written from origin develop `34cdcfb26` (read by `git ls-remote`; the #1035 KS-1204 squash, parent `3961c2add`). The test file
`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1213-a-derived-writer-relabel-is-refused.test.ts` (226 lines, blob `808282689`)
was read whole; the product file `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts` (blob `20934ee94`) was read at
`:185-:205` (the issue handler's destructuring, the KS-1213 guard and its refusal). KS-1229 and the #1031 tier-1 gate report (section
4 row X-ISSUE-LOOSE; section 9 D2) were read.

## THE MODE - read this twice

TEST-ONLY, MODIFY IN PLACE. This service runs JEST, not vitest: use `jest` names only, never `vi`. Your diff contains EXACTLY ONE
file: the EXISTING test file `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1213-a-derived-writer-relabel-is-refused.test.ts`,
with the ordinary header `--- a/Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1213-a-derived-writer-relabel-is-refused.test.ts` /
`+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1213-a-derived-writer-relabel-is-refused.test.ts` and ONE hunk.
**No hunk for `certifications.ts`.** Do NOT create a new test file. Do NOT copy the reference test - ignore it. The checker plants
the tamper named at the bottom into a clone of `certifications.ts` and expects the two new rows RED by assertion, then expects the
whole file GREEN at the untouched tip.

## What is wrong (one paragraph)

`POST /api/certifications/issue` with `parentDocumentId` refuses a `data.documentType` that differs from the certification type
(`:201`, 400 BAD_REQUEST). The guard tests `derivedDataDocumentType !== undefined`, so a NON-STRING carrier (a number, an array, an
object, a boolean) never equals the type and is refused - which is right, and matches the file's own header ("a non-string never
matches"). But the three issue RED rows in the ks1213 test all carry STRINGS, so loosening the guard to
`typeof derivedDataDocumentType === 'string'` keeps the whole originate suite green while a non-string is accepted: the #1031 gate
measured it (row X-ISSUE-LOOSE: 0 reds, 64 / 741; probe `7`, an array, an object, `true` -> 201, a stored certificate, the non-string
served). **This task:** two new rows in the EXISTING issue `it.each` table - a number carrier and an object carrier - so the existing
RED cell body (refused 400, nothing saved, no certification) pins them. No product line changes.

## Where (no product site changes - this list is informational; every line below STAYS)

- `:200` - (correct) `      const derivedDataDocumentType = data && typeof data === 'object' ? (data as Record<string, unknown>).documentType : undefined;` - the carrier is read as `unknown`, not narrowed to a string. Stays.
- `:201` - (correct) `      if (req.body.parentDocumentId && derivedDataDocumentType !== undefined && derivedDataDocumentType !== (type || 'verification_certificate')) {` - the KS-1213 issue guard. The tamper replaces this line. Stays.

## The exact change - ONE EDIT in the TEST file (one hunk, 3 lines of context each side)

E1 - INSERT two lines after line 184 (the third row of the issue `it.each` table, `['a case variant (type DOCUMENT, data.documentType
document)', ...],`) and before line 185 (the `])('RED %s: refused 400, ...` line that closes the table). Lines 182-184 above and lines
185-187 below stay (insert-after: the anchor is line 184, which is (correct) and stays):

```
     ['type DOCUMENT, data.documentType PROPERTY_DEED', { type: 'DOCUMENT', data: { title: 'c', documentType: 'PROPERTY_DEED' } }],
     ["type certificate, data.documentType DOCUMENT (the parent's type)", { type: 'certificate', data: { title: 'c', documentType: 'DOCUMENT' } }],
     ['a case variant (type DOCUMENT, data.documentType document)', { type: 'DOCUMENT', data: { title: 'c', documentType: 'document' } }],
+    ['a non-string number carrier (type DOCUMENT, data.documentType 7)', { type: 'DOCUMENT', data: { title: 'c', documentType: 7 } }], // KS-1229 X-ISSUE-LOOSE
+    ['an object carrier (type DOCUMENT, data.documentType an object)', { type: 'DOCUMENT', data: { title: 'c', documentType: { name: 'DOCUMENT' } } }], // KS-1229 X-ISSUE-LOOSE
   ])('RED %s: refused 400, no certification and no derived document written', async (_label, b) => {
     seed('DOCUMENT');
     expect(await issue({ ...b, parentDocumentId: SOURCE_ID })).toEqual(REFUSED);
```

The two `+` lines are byte-exact - copy them; do not paraphrase the labels, do not drop the trailing `// KS-1229 X-ISSUE-LOOSE`
comments (they are part of the line), do not re-indent (4 spaces before the `[`, exactly like the three rows above). The `7` is a
bare number, NOT the string `'7'`; the object is `{ name: 'DOCUMENT' }`, NOT a string. Every other line of the file stays
byte-identical. The rows add no new name: the existing cell body reads `seed`, `issue`, `SOURCE_ID`, `REFUSED` and
`mockSaveCertification`, all declared above. Do NOT import anything.

The `+` lines contain no non-ASCII character, no backslash, no dollar sign, no backtick and no double quote. Keep it that way. (The
context line 183 does carry double quotes - it is context, copy it unchanged.)

Red under the tamper: the tampered guard only refuses a STRING that differs, so the number row and the object row are accepted (201,
one derived document saved, a certification written) and each fails the existing `toEqual(REFUSED)` by assertion, on every principal.
Green at the tip: `7 !== 'DOCUMENT'` and `{ name: 'DOCUMENT' } !== 'DOCUMENT'`, so both are refused 400 with nothing saved. The three
existing string rows and the three controls stay green on both trees (a differing string is still refused; an equal string and no
`data.documentType` are still accepted).

## Red cells

- RED a non-string number carrier
- RED an object carrier

## Tamper (test-only mode - the checker plants this in a clone of certifications.ts to prove your new rows can go red)

line: 201
from: `      if (req.body.parentDocumentId && derivedDataDocumentType !== undefined && derivedDataDocumentType !== (type || 'verification_certificate')) {`
to: `      if (req.body.parentDocumentId && typeof derivedDataDocumentType === 'string' && derivedDataDocumentType !== (type || 'verification_certificate')) { // TAMPER: KS-1229 X-ISSUE-LOOSE red-proof, the gate's loosening - a non-string data.documentType is no longer refused`
statement_ok: the `from` line opens `if (...) {` whose body is `:202` (`return res.status(400).json({ ... BAD_REQUEST ... })`) and whose block closes at `:203`; nothing else is in the statement. The tamper changes ONE operand (`!== undefined` -> `typeof === 'string'`), so every string carrier behaves exactly as at the tip and only a non-string carrier changes from refused to accepted. `derivedDataDocumentType` is `unknown`, so the `typeof` guard compiles.

## Output

Exactly ONE ```diff block containing ONLY the modified test file: `--- a/Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1213-a-derived-writer-relabel-is-refused.test.ts`
then `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1213-a-derived-writer-relabel-is-refused.test.ts`, then ONE hunk:
`@@ -182,6 +182,8 @@` (six context lines, two `+` lines). No hunk for `certifications.ts` or any other file.

## Premises (measured)

All times AEST 2026-09-18, read from `date` in the script that produced them (`scratchpad/loose/run.sh`, session-local; outputs
`run.out`, `build_draft.out`, `prep.out`, `<variant>.checker.out`). Written IN-SEAT by Wednesday (the usage cut bars sub-agents).

- **P1 tip.** origin develop = `34cdcfb2663b9e4c31025044e6f842ad2c5a10a3` by `git ls-remote` on the Secuura checkout (04:07:13).
- **P2 the files at the tip.** ks1213 test blob `808282689` (226 lines; lines 182-187 read and compared against this brief's fence by a
  script: 6/6 context lines equal, a shifted-by-one control unequal); `certifications.ts` blob `20934ee94`; the tamper `from` line
  occurs exactly once (grep -c -F = 1). Both blobs are unchanged from `3961c2add` (the held KS-1229 brief's tip).
- **P3 the gap.** The #1031 tier-1 gate measured X-ISSUE-LOOSE directly (report
  `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1213-1031-be8596a29-tier1-r1/report.md` section 4): the loosening
  gives 0 reds, 64 / 741; probes `7`, an array, an object and `true` get 201, a stored certificate, and the non-string served. Not
  re-measured here (the gate's instrument, quoted).
- **P4 this brief's hunk through the REAL checker** (`tasks/code_patch/checker.sh`, draft input built rc 0 at 04:07:21,
  ~24.2K prompt tokens; own scratch clone at the tip, `prepare_clone.sh` rc 0): **RESULT PASS (7/7)** at 04:08:25. A2 strict; A3
  touched set = the ks1213 test only; A3c 2/2 and A3d clean; A3i 2 byte-exact; **A4 under the tamper 6 failed / 91, exactly the two
  declared rows x3 principals, by assertion**, controls green; A5 91/91 at the untouched tip; A6 originate 741 -> 747, no new red;
  A7 tsc rc 0.
- **P5 wrong variants through the real checker:** `stringseven` (the number row as the STRING `'7'`, a carrier the tamper still
  refuses) FAIL A3c (1 of 2 absent) at 04:08:39; `onlyone` (the object row dropped) FAIL A3c (1 of 2 absent) at 04:08:53. NOT run:
  `stringseven` with A3c emptied (whether A4 alone would catch a string carrier: predicted yes, unmeasured).
- **P6 source untouched.** `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` on the Secuura checkout = 0 at 04:07:08 and 04:08:53; only
  read verbs ran there (ls-remote, rev-parse, show, status); the clone is Wednesday's scratch (`git clone --shared`), porcelain 0 at end.
- **P7 partition.** Open-PR / seat-head / READY census NOT re-run for this brief: the held KS-1229 brief's census (01:00-01:17, 0 hits
  on this test file or `certifications.ts`) is 3 h old; since then #1035 (api-gateway `verification.ts` + its ks1204 test) and #1037
  (KS-1101) moved, neither in originate by their READY mails. The only known overlap is `READY_KS-1229_…-RECHECK` on the same file,
  hunk 204-209 (non-overlapping, see the raise notes).

  `Refs KS-1229 (X-ISSUE-AFTER-HOLDER, X-ISSUE-AFTER-ANCHOR, X-ISSUE-LOOSE)`, applying this one first or second with an offset.
- Still NOT briefed on KS-1229: X-SIGNCERT-AFTER-UPSTREAM, X-VERSION-TRIM, X-SIGNWALLET-SERVED (`documents.ts`),
